title: Safe string input, capacity, truncation and termination
learningObjectives: Use fgets with a buffer size to read bounded lines from a stream.
Explain how fgets stores a terminating null character and may retain a newline.
Check fgets return values before using the destination buffer.
Detect and handle input lines that exceed the available buffer capacity.
Avoid unsafe unbounded input and define a clear policy for truncation and invalid input.

understand.concept: Input routines must respect destination capacity and establish a valid terminator. fgets reads at most size minus one characters from a stream and, when it succeeds, stores a terminating null character. It retains a newline if one is read. A bounded read still requires a policy for detecting overlong lines, handling input failure and discarding or processing remaining characters.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Why input capacity matters

A character buffer has a fixed capacity. An input operation must never write more characters than the buffer can hold, including space for the null terminator. Unbounded input can overwrite adjacent memory and create serious vulnerabilities.

## 2. Read with fgets

`fgets(buffer, sizeof buffer, stdin)` reads at most one less than the buffer capacity, then appends a null character when it succeeds. If a newline is read before the limit, that newline is stored in the buffer.

## 3. Check the result

fgets returns the buffer pointer on success and a null pointer on failure or end-of-file before any characters are read. Do not inspect the destination as a newly read string unless the call succeeded.

## 4. Detect truncation

If the buffer does not contain a newline and the stream has not reached end-of-file, the line may be longer than the available space. Decide whether to reject the line, process it in chunks or discard the remainder before reading the next logical input line.

## 5. Validate content separately

A bounded read prevents writing beyond the supplied buffer when used correctly, but it does not validate the content. Check required fields, numeric ranges, encoding assumptions and trailing characters according to the application's input contract.

examples.title: Detect a missing newline
examples.explanation: A missing newline can indicate truncation, though a final line at end-of-file may legitimately have no newline. A production reader should define how to consume the remaining input.

practise.guidedTask: Implement a small C program demonstrating CL4.10. Identify the relevant array or string capacity, valid indices, expected results and failure cases before compiling and testing.
practise.independentTask: Create a second example for CL4.10 that handles a boundary case explicitly. Add tests for empty input, the smallest valid case, the largest valid case and one invalid or oversized case. Explain how your code prevents invalid access.
hints: Write down the exact array length and valid index range.
Include null terminator space when working with C strings.
Check function preconditions and return values.
Pass array lengths explicitly when a function needs them.

questions.prompt: How many input characters can fgets store in a buffer of size n, excluding the terminator?
questions.explanation: One element is reserved for the terminating null character.

questions.prompt: What does fgets do with a newline it reads?
options: It stores the newline in the buffer
It converts the newline to a null byte
questions.answer: It stores the newline in the buffer
questions.explanation: fgets retains a newline when it is read before the size limit.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before using a buffer after fgets?
options: Whether fgets returned a non-null pointer
Whether the buffer address is even
Whether the line contains a digit
questions.answer: Whether fgets returned a non-null pointer
questions.explanation: The return value indicates whether a line was read successfully.

questions.prompt: What can a missing newline in the buffer indicate?
options: The input line may have been longer than the available buffer
The compiler inserted an extra terminator
questions.answer: The input line may have been longer than the available buffer
questions.explanation: The buffer may have filled before the line ending was read.

questions.prompt: Does bounded input automatically validate the meaning of the text?
options: No; the application must still validate format and allowed values
Yes, it guarantees all input is valid
questions.answer: No; the application must still validate format and allowed values
questions.explanation: Capacity safety and semantic validation are separate responsibilities.
